items.issue: `has_invalid_unicode_scalar` never stops on cyclic input. It keeps no record of containers it has already visited, so a payload like `d = {"self": d}` loops forever and its pending list grows without limit. I checked this: `Observation(payload=d)` was still running after 3 s. Before this change the recursive copier raised `RecursionError`, and `RawFirstDecoder` turned that into a `raw.unknown` gap. Now a driver bug that builds a cyclic payload freezes the supervisor's decode path, along with the timeout and cleanup steps that wait on it. Both design reviewers raised this as a non-blocker. Fix: track the `id()` of containers already visited, either skipping them or raising `ValueError`. That is about 3 lines and keeps the scan iterative

items.issue: The R2 class of bug still exists at display time, outside this PRD's scope. `bounded_detail` strips only C0 controls and 7-bit CSI. The TUI's `display_text` drops all Cc/Cf/Cs/Zl/Zp characters (src/ovcaq/tui/model.py:57). Confirmed: `"lane sk-abc\u200b<36 chars>"` (also with \x85, \x9b, \u00ad, \u2060 instead of \u200b) passes redaction unchanged and the TUI shows the joined `sk-abcabcdef…` token. Activity text and tool details (src/ovcaq/drivers/codex_events.py:32, src/ovcaq/drivers/codex_events.py:127) strip nothing, so a NUL-split token also renders whole on screen. This needs a durable home (a PRD or issue)

items.issue: The pre-decode check assumes every driver parses frames with plain `json.loads`. A plugin driver that unwraps a prefix or applies its own escapes skips the pre-mutation check. The model still rejects the bad strings, so nothing crashes, but such a driver can change its state before the `Observation` constructor raises. Every frame (up to 1 MiB) is also parsed twice; the PRD sets no performance limit

items.issue: The review-1 two-pass `bounded_detail` leaks the tail of a split token. When the control sits after 20 or more body characters, pass 1 redacts the head. Control removal then glues the tail onto `[REDACTED]`, and pass 2 finds no `sk-` or `Bearer` prefix to match. I ran it to confirm: `bounded_detail('Diagnostic sk-abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz\x1b[0m0123456789ABCDEF')` returns `'Diagnostic [REDACTED]0123456789ABCDEF'`, the real `turn.failed` payload detail is the same, and `'Bearer '+'a'*23+'\x00bbbbbbbb'` returns `'Bearer [REDACTED]bbbbbbbb'`. Task 3's strip-first order redacted these fully, and pre-PRD code leaked the same way. This breaks two PRD rules ("ANSI/NUL splits of ordinary synthetic tokens are redacted", "synthetic credential fragments never enter normalized details") and makes docs/driver-protocol.md:224 claim too much. Every split test cuts at `token[:6]`, so no test catches it. Fix: before control removal, absorb token characters stuck to a marker across recognized controls with `re.sub(rf"\[REDACTED\](?:{controls})+[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+", "[REDACTED]", sanitize_text(protected))`. I probed this on both leaks plus `x\x00sk-…`, the OSC case and the cap reproducer, and all came out fully redacted (I did not run the suite with it). Also add SPLIT_DETAILS cases that split after 20 or more body characters, for both bare and Bearer tokens

items.issue: The `continue` at codex.py:383 drops every native update for a lane that has already finished. codex-cli 0.162.1 ships a `resume_agent` tool ("Resume a previously closed agent by id so it can receive send_input"; I confirmed the string in the binary). So a lane can legitimately go completed → close → resume → running → errored. With the `continue`, the resumed run's running and errored updates disappear with no trace, and a later interrupt or shutdown of the resumed run becomes raw unknown instead of `lane.failed`. The pre-change code reported these. The TUI already handles a restart, because the last write wins (src/ovcaq/tui/model.py:607). The PRD only requires that close statuses do not fail a completed lane, and the unfinished-only filter at src/ovcaq/drivers/codex.py:372 already does that on its own. Fix: delete lines 383-384. Then flip `test_finished_lane_late_update_retains_only_non_lane_observations` (tests/drivers/test_adapter_outcomes.py:266) so it expects running → `lane.progress` and errored → `lane.failed`, and reword docs/driver-protocol.md:243. Confidence: the tool is confirmed; the exact `agents_states` sequence after a resume is my guess
items.reason: Requirements ambiguity: resume/restart generation semantics are not specified by this PRD. The existing contract deliberately freezes completed/failed identities and pins late updates. A binary tool name does not prove a native status sequence; changing this would undo reviewed stability without a fixture. Preserve for separately specified adapter lifecycle work.

items.issue: The numeric grammar only accepts `HTTP[/x.y]`, `HTTP status [client|server error (]`, `status [code][:]` and `error code[:]`. Other explicit HTTP or error forms used to classify through the bare number and now return `unknown`. Confirmed by running the classifier: "HTTP Error 503: Service Unavailable" gives unknown (was connectivity), "HTTP Error 429: Too Many Requests" gives unknown (was rate_limit), "Error 403: Forbidden" gives unknown (was permission), "status=429" gives unknown. The tests pin `status=429` and `Error 429:` as UNKNOWN. Codex's own Rust forms (`unexpected status N ...`, `last status: N`, reqwest `HTTP status ... error (N ...)`) are covered, so the risk is limited to non-native formats.

items.issue: A completed lane can still turn into a failure after the identity cache fills. At 4096 entries, eviction drops finished entries first, so long sessions lose finished lanes before anything else. Reproduced: start lane `child`, complete it, decode 4096 command items, then send a late `errored` update for `child`. The decoder emits `lane.failed` for `child`, alongside the raw capacity-gap evidence. Native Codex is unlikely to send `errored` after `completed`, so the practical risk is low.

items.issue: Numeric diagnostics now need "HTTP", "HTTP status", "status code" or "error code" (src/ovcaq/drivers/codex_events.py:301), so Codex's own status wording falls to UNKNOWN. I ran `classify_failure` on "unexpected status 503 Service Unavailable", "unexpected status 502 Bad Gateway", "unexpected status 403 Forbidden" and "exceeded retry limit, last status: 429 Too Many Requests", and all four return `unknown`. The old code returned connectivity, permission and rate_limit for these. Both prefixes are confirmed as strings in the installed codex 0.162.1 binary; the "503 Service Unavailable" suffix is my guess at how Codex renders the code. Effect: 502/503 skip the bounded connectivity WAIT and get an immediate died-retry and then PARK, and 403 retries instead of halting for the operator. The PRD allows "HTTP/status/error-code" context, and "status 503" is a status context. Fix: accept a bare `status` (e.g. `(?:http(?: status)? | status(?: code)? | error code)`) and add both Codex spellings as literal positives in tests/drivers/test_adapter_failure_classes.py:55

items.issue: The recovery fix still leaves one gap in the exit race. After `cleanup_run_records` removes run.json, the supervisor process stays alive until the interpreter exits. A poll in that gap gets `ended=False`, an idle observation with `run_id=None`, and `state=None`. Because that identity no longer matches the selected run, `_observe` closes the follower and clears the session cache. The next poll is terminal but has no `_session_id`, so the final frame loses lanes, activity and provider. I confirmed this with a probe: I ran `Selected.finish()`, forced `_run_observation.process_matches` to return True for one poll, and polled again. `assert_final_telemetry` then failed with `'unknown' == 'selected-provider'`. The new tests miss this because `finish()` waits for the process to exit fully. Fix: clear the cache only when `selected.ended` is true or the observation shows a different active run (`observation.run_id` is not None and differs). Missing metadata alone should not clear it.
items.reason: Confirmed cleanup-before-process-exit cache-loss edge. This predates and remains outside the activity projection contract; changing behavior when selected ownership metadata is absent needs a separate fail-closed observer contract covering replacement and malformed identities. Preserve the reported defect and probe; do not apply the suggested relaxed identity guard opportunistically. Correct consensus is Alice 1/3: Blake reported scope, Bob requested identity-guard coverage, not this defect.
